title: Insulation Rebates in Rochester, NY (2026): RG&E Area, EmPower+, Comfort Home
desc: Rochester insulation help for 2026: the city is served by RG&E, not National Grid. EmPower+ up to $12,000 for low-income homes, Comfort Home $2,500 to $3,000, and an RG&E heat pump rebate that rises after insulating.
lead: First, a correction many sites get wrong: the City of Rochester gets its power and gas from RG&E, not National Grid. That changes which utility programs apply. Here is the insulation help a Rochester home can get in 2026, and how it can raise an RG&E heat pump rebate by $5,000.
cards_heading: What insulation help exists in Rochester
cards_intro: We re-read NYSERDA's EmPower+ and Comfort Home pages and the NYS Clean Heat manual on October 3, 2026. RG&E's own website did not load for us that day, so check RG&E's current insulation offer with them directly.

cards.title: EmPower+ low income
cards.note: No-cost insulation, air sealing and safety work for income-eligible owners and renters of 1 to 4 family homes. Monroe County uses the upstate cap.

cards.title: EmPower+ moderate income
cards.note: Plus up to $1,600 in federal HEAR money for air sealing, insulation and ventilation.

cards.title: NYSERDA Comfort Home
cards.note: Good and Better seal and insulate packages, plus $2,000 for windows afterward. Any income.

cards.title: RG&E Home Insulation and Air Sealing
cards.note: Named in the NYS Clean Heat manual as an approved weatherization program for the Weatherized Tier. We could not read RG&E's page to confirm current amounts.

after_cards:
Working it out with RG&E numbers

For an RG&E single-family home that installs a heat pump and removes the old system, NYS Clean Heat pays $7,000. After an approved weatherization program, the Weatherized Tier pays $12,000. In a Disadvantaged Community it is $8,000, or $13,000 weatherized. A $3,000 Comfort Home Better package can therefore be worth $8,000 in total.
sections:
The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts about 104,500 homes in Rochester. 87% were built before 1980 and 54% in 1939 or earlier. 44% are single detached houses, a higher share than Buffalo or Syracuse, and 26% are in buildings of 2 to 4 units. About 38% of households own their home.

72% of homes heat with piped gas and 22% with electricity. So most Rochester homeowners are sealing and insulating to cut a gas bill, while about one in five is fighting an electric heating bill, where the payback is quicker.

Rochester sits under National Grid in our site's address, but RG&E is the utility. Programs from National Grid, like its Weatherization Health and Safety Program, are for National Grid customers. Your Clean Heat rebate also follows RG&E's table, which shares its numbers with NYSEG. Check the name on your bill before you apply for anything. Our NYSEG and RG&E rebates page has the details.
Three routes to the Weatherized Tier

The NYS Clean Heat manual gives three ways to qualify for the higher heat pump rebate. One: the home was built after 2010. Two: the home went through an approved program, which for RG&E customers includes RG&E's Home Insulation and Air Sealing or NYSERDA's Comfort Home. Three: the home passes a heating-load test based on its size. With 54% of Rochester homes built before 1940, the first route rarely applies, so a program is the usual path.

About 62% of Rochester households rent. EmPower+ is open to income-eligible renters of 1 to 4 family homes, with the landlord's okay. If you heat with electricity and pay the bill, show your landlord the numbers above.
claim_heading: How to get insulation help in Rochester
claim_steps: Check your bill. If it says RG&E, use RG&E and NYSERDA programs.
Check EmPower+ income limits for Monroe County and apply on the MyEnergy portal if you qualify.
If not, look up Comfort Home contractors for Monroe County, or call RG&E about its insulation and air sealing program.
Keep your completion paperwork for the Clean Heat Weatherized Tier.
faq: Is Rochester served by National Grid?
No. The City of Rochester is served by RG&E. National Grid serves other parts of upstate New York, like Buffalo, Syracuse and Albany.
How much more is the RG&E heat pump rebate after insulating?
For a single-family home with old-system removal, $12,000 instead of $7,000, per the NYS Clean Heat manual. In a Disadvantaged Community, $13,000 instead of $8,000.
$2,500 for the Good package, $3,000 for the Better package, and $2,000 for windows after sealing and insulation.
Is insulation free for low-income Rochester families?
Through EmPower+, income-eligible households can get no-cost work up to $12,000 per project upstate.
Is there a federal tax credit for insulation in 2026?
No. The IRS says the 25C credit does not apply to work placed in service after December 31, 2025.
